name: Dienedione
lead: Dienedione (estra-4,9-diene-3,17-dione) is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid of the 19-nortestosterone group that was never medically used. It was sold as a bodybuilding supplement, often marketed as a trenbolone prohormone, to people hoping to add muscle mass and a harder, leaner look [1].

Wikipedia describes it as thought to be a prohormone of dienolone, a compound structurally almost identical to trenbolone but lacking the C11 double bond [1]. That relationship is why the product was positioned as a trenbolone-like supplement; no human studies of its effect on muscle exist.
It became a US Schedule III steroid on January 4, 2010 and is Class C in the UK [1]. The published research is about doping control, particularly in horses [2][3][4].

paras: Before scheduling, dienedione was sold in the US as a dietary supplement for bodybuilding, frequently described as a trenbolone prohormone [1]. It never had a medical use [1].

Dienedione is a 19-nortestosterone-derived androgen receptor agonist thought to act as a prohormone of dienolone [1]. Wikipedia provides no receptor-binding, potency or pharmacokinetic data for it [1].

Dienedione is mainly an intermediate in the synthesis of trenbolone, mifepristone, ulipristal and dienogest, among other steroids such as altrenogest and trimegestone [1]. Organon patents from 1999 cover a synthesis route from a soy phytosterol-derived starting material (Sitolactone) [1]. Mifepristone (RU 486) is the antiprogestin whose pharmacology was studied in the 1980s in contraception and in Cushing's syndrome [5][6]; those papers concern mifepristone, not dienedione itself.

It became a Schedule III anabolic steroid in the US under the Controlled Substances Act on January 4, 2010, and is Class C in the UK [1]. It is prohibited in human and equine sport [2]. A list of banned substances quoted in a 2020 T Nation thread on natural bodybuilding contests includes estra-4,9-diene-3,17-dione [7].

In the US it was sold as a supplement, and some products were seized in FDA enforcement action related to Bodybuilding.com for selling unapproved new drugs; Wikipedia cites an FDA enforcement report dated 7 July 2010 [1].

A 2025 study in Drug Testing and Analysis reported that dienedione is detected in the urine of entire male horses and investigated whether it is endogenous in that species; Wikipedia summarises this as finding small natural production in intact male horses [1][2]. Further papers addressed doping control and hair monitoring in horses [3][4].

timeline.event: Becomes a US Schedule III steroid on 4 January; FDA enforcement action involving supplement sales is reported in July.[1]
Study reports endogenous nature in male horses.[2]

card.summary: A trenbolone-type prohormone sold as a supplement until it was scheduled in 2010; no human studies exist.

quick.overview:
Dienedione is a 19-nortestosterone steroid that was sold as a bodybuilding prohormone. It was scheduled in the US in 2010.

Research is limited to doping control, notably in horses.
quick.mechanism: It is thought to act as a prohormone to dienolone, a compound structurally close to trenbolone.
quick.risks: No human safety data. Controlled in the US and UK and prohibited in sport.

chain: Oral prohormone taken as a supplement
Thought to convert to dienolone, a trenbolone-like androgen
Claimed muscle gain and leaner look
angle.text: Supplement users sought a trenbolone-like effect on muscle and leanness from an over-the-counter pill. The conversion pathway is described on Wikipedia as thought rather than measured in published human studies.
